title: Per-Token Economics & Latency Dashboard - Wireframes + Grooming
content:
Context and goals:

This doc collects UX notes, wireframe iterations, and backlog grooming items for a new Console dashboard that surfaces per-token cost and latency breakdowns. Goal: give engineers + platform owners a clear, actionable view into where tokens and time are spent so they can reduce unit cost and meet latency SLOs without guessing.

Primary user personas:
- Platform Engineer (SRE/infra): needs latency percentiles and hot routes (A->B) to tune autoscaling, identify tail sources.
- Product Engineer (feature owner): wants per-route cost attribution, quick drilldowns to offending prompts, and suggestions to reduce prompt tokens.
- Finance/PM: monthly slices of token spend by product and model family, exportable CSV.

High-level metrics to surface (ranked):
1) Per-token cost (USD per token) aggregated by route/model/time window and token role (system/user/assistant/kv-overhead).
2) Latency distributions (p50/p90/p99) and a fine-grained waterfall for inference phases (preprocessing, model forward, tokenization, streaming overhead, postprocessing).
3) Token flow visualization (Sankey-style) showing where tokens originate and how they map to billed tokens and generation tokens.
4) Route-level cost per successful response and cost per 1000 tokens, with filters by model and deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
5) Query-level drilldown showing raw prompt, tokenized counts, token types, per-step timing, and an estimated cost breakdown.

Core UX principles:
- Start simple: default view = top 10 routes by spend last 24h.
- Fast drilldown: click a route -> show sample queries (paginated) with copyable prompt, tokenization preview, and the timeline for that request.
- Compare mode: two time windows side-by-side (baseline vs current) to visualize regressions after model changes or rollouts.
- Actionable suggestions: tie Optimize recommendations (quantization, batching, response-length hints) to a route and show potential savings.

Wireframe iterations (notes + intent):

Iteration A (early sketch) - Overview + Sankey:
- Top bar: timeframe selector, percentile slider (p50/p90/p99), model family dropdown, export CSV button.
- Main left: stacked bar list of top routes by $/day (each bar split by token category colors: system/user/instruction/generation/kv-overhead). Hover shows absolute token counts and per-token cost.
- Main right: Sankey diagram mapping token sources -> internal overhead -> billed tokens. Hover on a flow highlights downstream latency impact.
- Bottom: small latency histogram (interactive) and a link to open a request sampler panel.
- Notes: Sankey is visually compelling but expensive to render for many routes; show for selected route only.

Iteration B - Route Detail Panel (drilldown):
- Left: selected route header (route ID, model pinned, deployment type, 24h spend).
- Center: micro-waterfall chart (bars for tokenization, kv lookup, infer-forward per chunk, streaming buffer, postprocess). Each bar is hoverable to show median and tail times.
- Right: token table (columns: token-type, count, % of total, estimated cost). Rows expandable to list example tokens (hashed) and link to raw prompt.
- Actions: "Suggest trim" (opens quick-editor with suggested prompt edits), "Pin as expensive" (adds to alerting rules), "Request sample export".

Iteration C - Compare + Hypothesis Mode:
- Two-pane compare for baseline vs current. Color-coded deltas for token counts and latency percentiles.
- Quick A/B note field for product owners to annotate suspected causes (model swap, rollout fraction, config change).

Interaction details and microcopy notes:
- Tooltip on per-token cost: "Per-token cost is an attribution based on model pricing and observed tokenization. It excludes infra amortized costs unless toggled on in advanced settings."
- Edge cases: when response streaming adds overhead, show both streaming latency and generation time (they can differ).
- Missing token taxonomy: if we cannot reliably split system vs user tokens (e.g., encrypted inputs), mark as "uncategorized" and show a confidence score.

Performance and data model considerations (UX implications):
- Avoid rendering per-request Sankeys by default; use aggregated buckets and allow sampling for request-level Sankeys.
- Backend must supply: token counts by role, per-phase timing histograms, and sample request ids. We will rely on existing telemetry (INF telemetry pipeline) with additional token-type tagging.
- UI should support server-side pagination and precomputed percentile ranges for fast render.

Backlog grooming (stories, estimates, acceptance criteria):

1) INF-2314: Dashboard MVP - top routes by spend + per-token stacked bars (5 pts)
   - Owner: Jin Park
   - Acceptance: default timeframe loads within 2s, bars show token split, export CSV includes per-route token counts.

2) INF-2330: Route drilldown - micro-waterfall + token table (8 pts)
   - Owner: Ruth Gomez
   - Acceptance: drilldown panel opens in <500ms for selected route; micro-waterfall shows p50/p90, token table rows expand.

3) INF-2350: Request sampler and sample Sankey (3 pts)
   - Owner: Liam O'Connor
   - Acceptance: sampling modal returns 10 example requests for selected route, Sankey renders, and clicking a node highlights related timeline.

4) INF-2372: Compare mode + annotation notes (5 pts)
   - Owner: Kai Zhang
   - Acceptance: user can select two non-overlapping windows, see delta overlay, save annotation linked to route.

5) INF-2410: Optimize integration - show potential savings and one-click suggestion flow (8 pts)
   - Owner: product-console
   - Acceptance: suggestions compute estimated % cost reduction and create a task in Optimize pipeline.

Low-priority / nice-to-have:
- Token heatmap by hour-of-day (2 pts).
- Per-tenant cost allocation toggles for enterprise billing (4 pts).
- Auto-detection of prompt bloat patterns (e.g., repeated system messages) + auto-suggest trimming (6 pts).

Open questions and tradeoffs (to resolve in grooming):
- Pricing model attribution: do we show raw model list prices or include infra amortization? (Impacts accuracy vs simplicity.)
- Sankey fidelity vs performance: sample-based Sankey vs aggregated approximate flows?
- Privacy: stored sample prompts may contain PII. Need to default to redaction and make sampling opt-in for private deployments.

Experimental UX tests we should run:
- Does a Sankey (visual flow) improve triage time vs a numeric table? Run with SREs on 10 incidents and measure time-to-root-cause.
- Do suggested prompt edits reduce cost without harming quality? Small A/B on non-critical routes.

Short-term next steps (owner/actions):
- Jin: mock up static Figma screens for Iteration A + B by 2026-03-02.
- Ruth: confirm telemetry fields available with infra (INF-telemetry channel) and add missing tags by 2026-03-05.
- Asha: schedule walk-in review with SRE and two product owners (2026-03-04).
- Kai: draft acceptance tests and export cases for finance.

Notes to self / meeting fragments (rough):
- "If we show model price + effective per-token cost, folks will immediately blame the model rather than the prompt. Need friction: show both but surface suggested actions."
- "We should align with billing team on per-tenant overrides before enabling exportable chargeback."

Appendix: short copy snippets for UI
- Empty state for routes: "No high-spend routes in selected window. Try expanding timeframe or lowering percentile slider."
- Row action label: "Investigate (sample requests)"
- Micro-waterfall tooltip: "Median time for tokenization (ms)"

This is a working doc — expect many iterations. Use linked JIRA tickets for formal prioritization. Will convert selected Figma frames into a handoff spec once Iteration B is locked.
